collaborators.name: ChatGPT
collaborators.requested: GPT-6, High Effort, regular chat mode (chosen in the ChatGPT app; not verifiable from here)
collaborators.role: Architecture, advanced reasoning, code review, debugging, gameplay improvements, creative direction
asks: Review the simulation architecture (src/sim): is the split between pure rules and rendering sound, and is anything going to hurt us once the renderer, input and UI are attached?
Hunt for logic bugs in game.js and world.js: hop/landing on logs and lily pads, collisions mid-hop, the camera creep and eagle, the input buffer. Point at exact lines.

Challenge the big design decision in STATUS.md: the chicken hops TOWARD the camera (down the screen) so the man's face is always visible. Is there a better way to keep the face visible? Argue for or against it.
Difficulty curve: look at difficulty(), the lane mix and the speeds/gaps in world.js. Suggest concrete number changes for the first 60 seconds of play and for row 150+.
Creative direction: game-over lines, a better title than 'Beanie Hop' if you have one, and one or two replayability ideas that fit the photo-face concept.

api.note: Off: needs an OpenAI API key, and this environment blocks api.openai.com. Copy-and-paste route in use.

collaborators.name: Gemini
collaborators.requested: Gemini Neon 4 High in Antigravity. Running instead: gemini-3.8-flash at high reasoning effort through the Gemini API free tier (Neon needs paid billing)
collaborators.role: Visual design, graphics, animation, performance optimisation, independent testing
asks: Face integration (no images this round, for privacy; work from the code): src/render/chicken.js puts the face texture on the front of a 0.64 x 0.78 x 0.56 head box, with a knit beanie on the top and sides, a comb, a beak and a wattle under the chin, and emissiveIntensity 0.32. Will this read as part of the chicken's head rather than a picture stuck on it? Give specific changes (proportions, positions, shading, materials).
tools/make_face.py: review the colour grade, mask feathering, contact shadow and crop maths. The face will be about 40 CSS pixels wide on a phone. What would keep the man recognisable at that size?
Palette and models (models.js, lanes.js): does the world look cohesive and readable at a glance (cars vs logs vs trains vs safe grass)? Name the exact PAL colours or model sizes you would change.
Animation: the hop, squash-and-stretch, wing flap, idle and death poses in chicken.js. What would make them feel better?
Mobile performance: draw calls, shadow cost, materials, the instanced particles, the edgeShade shader patch. What will hurt on a mid-range Android phone?

api.note: Free tier: no cost, but Google may use what is sent to improve its products, so send code only, never the photo.

collaborators.name: Grok
collaborators.requested: Grok in Cursor, 4.7 Expert (chosen in Cursor; not verifiable from here)
collaborators.role: Gameplay mechanics, code optimisation, edge-case detection, independent technical review
asks: Find edge cases that break or cheat the rules: hopping off a log at the playfield edge, sideways hops on logs, landing exactly on a log's end, bumping while riding a log, trains arriving mid-hop, inputs queued at the moment of death, going backwards past the camera.
Find any seed and row where the level is impossible or unfair (use the generator and the bot; tests/sim.test.js shows how). Give the seed and row so it can be reproduced.
Write at least two new failing tests in the style of tests/sim.test.js for any bug you find (paste them in your reply).
Optimisation: anything in step(), landingSpot(), vehicleAt() or the bot that is wasteful at 120 steps per second on a phone?
Mechanics: are HOP_TIME, the input buffer (QUEUE_MAX), LOG_TOLERANCE, EAGLE_MARGIN and autoScroll() tuned well for touch controls? Propose values with reasons.
